title: Voronoi Map Generator: Nearest-Site Territories
description: Generate a Voronoi map from seed points with the Voronoi Map Generator — every place coloured by its nearest site. Free.
summary_sentence: For example, with seeds in New York, Boston and Philadelphia, Hartford falls in Boston's cell — 92.4 miles from Boston against 100.4 from New York — so Boston is its nearest-site territory.
quick_answer: The Voronoi Map Generator divides a map into territories around seed points, where every spot belongs to the seed it is nearest to. Drop your sites and generate the cells: the cleanest possible picture of natural catchments, service territories and 'which location serves this address?' — answered by geometry alone.

Perpendicular bisectors you can see: every cell edge is the set of points equidistant from two seeds. Voronoi is the rare maths topic that explains itself in one picture.

Hartford is closer to Boston (92.4 mi) than to New York (100.4 mi) as the crow flies, so it wears Boston's colour — despite every cultural instinct saying otherwise. Straight-line territory is honest about distance and blind to highways; both halves of that sentence matter.

examples.label: Example · The border is a bisector

body.t: Between two seeds, the cell border is the perpendicular bisector of the segment joining them: every border point is exactly equidistant from both. Move a seed and the whole neighbourhood's borders swing — the map is a machine for what-if.

faq: Which distance does it use — straight or road?
Straight-line proximity: each point joins its geometrically nearest seed. Road and drive-time territories are different, deliberately — compare both before signing a franchise map.
What happens with two seeds at the same spot?
They share one cell between them (an exact tie along no border at all). Nudge duplicates apart or merge them — the generator treats coincidence literally.
Can cells be clipped to a boundary?
Territory work usually clips cells to a coastline, county or trade area — the unclipped cell is the raw geometry; clipping is presentation with legal consequences, so it is a deliberate step.
Weighted Voronoi exists (additive and multiplicative forms) for exactly that. The standard map here is the unweighted classic — know which your decision needs.
From a handful to a few hundred reads clearly. Thousands become a texture, not a map — aggregate first, as the base FAQ's seed question suggests.
The cells are ordinary polygons conceptually — export paths follow the creation tools' formats, and GIS Voronoi (Thiessen) tools reproduce the geometry natively for verification.
Is this how phone coverage works?
Conceptually, towers' nearest-areas sketch coverage — real coverage follows signal propagation, not pure distance. The map is the intuition, not the engineering.
